hook: You think play is just a childish waste of time.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You think play is just a childish waste of time. Ancient thinkers actually saw play as a deep instinct shared by all living creatures. In 2015, neuroscientist Gordon Burghardt at the University of Tennessee studied animal behavior across species over several decades. He found that even reptiles, fish, and spiders engage in play purely for emotional satisfaction. It is not just one group of animals either. Studies across the globe reveal this universal drive, known in biology as surplus energy theory. So why do we assume animals only act for basic survival? Science shows that play triggers dopamine pathways, proving that joy is an evolutionary necessity rather than a luxury. The result? Animals actively seek fun just to feel good. That's it. When rats are tickled, they emit ultrasonic laughter. When ravens slide down snowy roofs, they do it for sheer pleasure. So next time you take a break to have fun, remember you think play is just a childish waste of time.

claims.claim: Reptiles, fish, and invertebrates engage in play behavior for intrinsic motivation and satisfaction.
Rats emit ultrasonic vocalizations resembling laughter when engaged in play and tickling.

theme: How Animals Show Joy Through Play
